methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $20M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Amperon is a Series B-stage infrastructure and logistics company founded by Sean Kelly. The company has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of direct public or private comparable companies in the dataset, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology alone.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $20M total capital raised, reflecting typical step-up dynamics between Series B and the subsequent financing round. This approach yields an implied valuation of $38M. Given the single-method constraint and inherent range around stage-based multipliers, the analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $44M, with $38M representing the median point.

The primary uncertainty stems from reliance on a single valuation methodology. A more robust analysis would require comparable company multiples—either from public peers or later-stage private transactions in infrastructure and logistics—to validate or adjust the stage-progression output. The applicability of the 1.9x multiplier depends on Amperon's specific growth profile, market position, and unit economics relative to typical Series B companies in this sector. Until additional comp data or company-specific metrics become available, this range should be treated as preliminary and subject to material revision.
